messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Each 5-ng/mL higher first-trimester 25(OH)D was associated with lower odds of EPDS-positive postpartum depressive symptoms in the crude model.
Sentence: "Each 5-ng/mL increase in 25(OH)D was associated with lower odds of EPDS-positive symptoms in the crude model (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.25-0.48) and after adjustment for baseline characteristics (adjusted OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.25-0.50)."
Measured as: EPDS-positive postpartum depressive symptoms
Population: 242 women with gestational diabetes mellitus
Intervention: First-trimester serum 25(OH)D concentration (per 5 ng/mL increase)
Comparator: Lower 25(OH)D levels
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 242
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational cohorts linking vitamin D level to depression, but they differ in population (post-COVID inpatients vs gestational diabetes women) and depression measure (PHQ-9 >5 at 6 months vs postpartum EPDS), and Study A's direction is not stated in the abstract.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: post-COVID hospital patients (n=72) vs women with gestational diabetes in the postpartum period (n=242); instruments PHQ-9 vs EPDS"}
